references.text: Moses reminds the people that they have been rebellious against the Lord from the day they left Egypt, highlighting their ongoing rebellion.
Moses testifies to Israel's stubbornness and rebellion against the Lord throughout their journey, predicting that this will continue after his death.
The Lord describes Israel as a stiff-necked people, reflecting their persistent rebellion mentioned in Deuteronomy.
Isaiah describes how the people were rebellious and grieved the Holy Spirit of the Lord, reflecting the same pattern of rebellion.
Ezekiel is sent to a stubborn people who have rebelled against the Lord, continuing the theme of Israel's ongoing disobedience.
Stephen accuses the Jews of being stiff-necked and always resisting the Holy Spirit, just as their ancestors did.
The psalmist describes how the fathers did not understand the Lord's wonders in Egypt and rebelled at the sea.
